title: 4th of July Berry Swirl Cupcakes
shortDescription: Vanilla cupcakes with a red and blue berry swirl frosting, ready in about 45 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes baking.
description: These cupcakes bring the fireworks straight to your dessert table. A soft vanilla cake holds up a swirled frosting made from real strawberry and blueberry purees, no food coloring needed. I tested this batch for a backyard cookout last summer and the red and blue swirl got more photos than the fireworks did. The trick is keeping both purees thick so they pipe clean lines instead of blending into purple mush. You pipe two colors side by side in one piping bag, so each cupcake gets its own unique swirl pattern. It looks fancy but the method is simple once you see the steps. This recipe works great for block parties, potlucks, or any patriotic holiday where you want a homemade treat that still travels well in a cupcake carrier.
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
1/4 cup fresh strawberry puree, strained and reduced
1/4 cup fresh blueberry puree, strained and reduced
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together for 3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Add flour mix and milk in three additions, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners and bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat butter for frosting until pale, then add powdered sugar in two batches with the cream and vanilla. Beat until smooth and thick.
Split frosting into two bowls. Mix strawberry puree into one and blueberry puree into the other, until each is stiff enough to hold a swirl.
Line a piping bag with a large star tip, then spoon red frosting down one side and blue down the other side of the bag.
Pipe a tall swirl on each cooled cupcake, working from the outside in so both colors show.
tips: Reduce your berry purees over low heat until thick like jam, so the frosting does not turn runny.
Chill the loaded piping bag for 10 minutes if the kitchen is warm, it holds the swirl shape better.
Use gel-free purees, not juice or syrup, or the frosting colors will bleed together.
Make the cupcakes a day ahead and frost them the morning of your party for the freshest look.

faq.question: Can I use frozen berries for the purees?
faq.answer: Yes, thaw them fully and drain extra liquid before blending. Cook the puree a bit longer to thicken it since frozen berries release more water.

faq.question: Why did my swirl turn purple instead of staying red and blue?
faq.answer: This happens when the purees are too thin and blend inside the piping bag. Reduce each puree until thick, then keep them on opposite sides of the bag.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead for a 4th of July party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them covered at room temperature. Make the frosting fresh the same day for the best color and texture.

faq.question: Do I need a special piping tip for the two-tone swirl?
faq.answer: A large open star tip works best for a clean swirl pattern. A round tip will still show two colors but with a smoother, less defined look.

conclusion: These berry swirl cupcakes turn a simple vanilla base into a holiday centerpiece. Once you get the two-tone piping down, you can use the same trick for any patriotic party.
